title: Where is it? In, on, under, left, right

parent.learn: Inside – outside, on – under, above – below.
parent.why: These words say where something is. The child needs them to follow directions like “put it under the bed”.

parent.learn: In front of – behind, near – far.
parent.why: In a queue, the person in front goes first. Far things look smaller — that is why the moon looks tiny.

parent.learn: First, middle, last in a row.
parent.why: Order words help with queues, stories and later with ordinal numbers (1st, 2nd, 3rd).
We read and write from left to right, so knowing left is needed for reading. A trick: hold up both hands, thumb out — the left hand makes an “L”.

ask: Put the teddy under the table. Now on the table. Now behind it.
What is above your head right now?
Raise your right hand. Touch your left ear.
Who is in front of you in the line? Who is behind?
Is the window near or far from you?
Line up three toys: which is first, middle, last?
What is inside your school bag?

rounds.t: The bird flies high in the sky. Is it up or down?
rounds.h: The sky is above us — up.
Fish swim inside the water: in.

rounds.t: When it rains, we stand ___ the umbrella.
rounds.h: The umbrella is above us and we stay dry below it: under.
The sock covers the foot, so the foot is inside.

rounds.t: The roof is on the ___ of the house.
rounds.h: The roof covers the house from above — the top.

rounds.t: In a queue, Asha is first and Bina is next. Who is in front?
rounds.h: First in the queue means in front of everyone.

rounds.t: The moon looks small because it is very ___
rounds.h: Things far away look smaller. The moon is very far from us.

rounds.t: At night you sleep ___ a blanket.
rounds.h: The blanket is on top of you; you are under it.

rounds.t: What is the opposite of near?
rounds.h: Near means close by; far means a long way away.
Your nose is on your face — the nearest thing of all!

rounds.t: Which fruit is on the left?
rounds.h: We start on the left, like reading. The apple comes first.

rounds.t: Which fruit is in the middle?
rounds.h: The banana has one fruit on each side, so it is in the middle.

rounds.t: Which fruit is on the right?
rounds.h: The grapes are at the right end, last when reading.

rounds.t: Which animal is just after the cat?
rounds.h: Reading left to right: dog, cat, mouse, rabbit. The mouse comes right after the cat.
English words go from the left side of the page to the right.
